author: Tom Gayner
title: Markel Group 2025 Letter to Shareholders
headline: Gayner: intrinsic value per share up 12% in 2025, insurance decentralised again under a new CEO, reinsurance sold off.
summary: Markel’s intrinsic value per share grew 12% in 2025, 15% a year over five years and 16% a year since its IPO. Operating revenues reached $15.5 billion, the combined ratio was 94% and reserves proved redundant for the 21st year in a row. Gayner admits insurance had become too centralised; the new insurance CEO, Simon Wilson, is moving decisions back to the front line, and Markel sold the renewal rights of its reinsurance business. Public equities returned 10.5%, 223,000 shares were bought back at an average $1,894, and the bond portfolio stays clear of private credit. The industrial businesses slowed in a “K-shaped” economy.

takeaways.label: Move
takeaways.text: Sold the renewal rights of the reinsurance business to focus on specialty insurance, where Markel has an edge.

takeaways.label: Move
takeaways.text: Bought back 223,000 shares at an average $1,894; the share count fell from about 14 million in 2016 to 12.6 million.

takeaways.label: View
takeaways.text: No private credit or riskier credit in the bond portfolio: those bonds are there to pay claims.

takeaways.label: Watch
takeaways.text: Tougher economic conditions and softer property insurance prices may weigh on reported results in the short run.

risks.text: A “K-shaped” economy: businesses outside the AI spending boom face tougher end markets.
Running off the reinsurance book temporarily raises the expense ratio and lowers revenue.

quotes.text: We don’t stretch for extra basis points of yield that might jeopardize that in any way, shape, or form.
While some investors will run faster over the sprint distances of a year or three, we operate as if we are running a marathon.

stocks.note: Its own shares, bought back at an average $1,894.
